resources.string: Start NetWatch with --agent on your home server or PC. It prints a link like https://192.168.1.10:8765/?token=… and a SHA-256 fingerprint. Paste the whole link here.
This doesn\'t look like an agent link. It must start with https:// and contain ?token=
Could not reach the agent: %1$s\n\nAre you on the same network as the agent?
The agent refused the token. Copy the link again from the agent\'s output (or data/agent-token).

The agent presented this certificate:

%1$s

Does it match the SHA-256 fingerprint the agent printed when it started? If it doesn't, someone may be intercepting the connection.
The agent\'s certificate changed. The connection was blocked. If you regenerated the certificate, choose “Change agent”.

A quick, user-started check of common service ports on your current private Wi-Fi subnet. It does not download data.

Connect to an optional NetWatch agent for whole-network monitoring, history and alerts.
The standalone checks run on this phone. Android does not let an ordinary app passively capture every device’s traffic on the Wi-Fi network.
Checks the current Wi-Fi protection mode, router, DNS servers and Android’s internet validation. Router identity cannot be proven by these checks.
Run a check when you are ready.
Looks up DNS, checks the HTTPS certificate and selected security headers. Sends a HEAD request only and does not follow redirects.
Read-only DNS check for SPF and DMARC. Use a domain you manage; no email is sent.
